nodes.label: Serverless client-first chess application
nodes.description: Real-time online 1v1 chess app on Firebase; rules run in the browser, position is stored in Realtime Database, and database rules enforce turn ownership.

nodes.label: 10x10 GridBoard with central 8x8
nodes.description: The board uses a 10x10 matrix with the standard 8x8 playable area centered and 36 locked border squares reserved for later expansion.

nodes.label: Firebase Realtime Database sync
nodes.description: Client-side Firebase SDK synchronizes rooms, board state, move history, clocks, and presence without backend logic.

nodes.label: IChessEngine abstraction
nodes.description: Unified engine interface exposing initialization, legal moves, move execution, FEN, turn, and game-over state so a variant adapter can replace the standard engine.

nodes.label: StandardEngine chessops adapter
nodes.description: Phase 1 engine adapter that parses FEN, checks legal chessops moves, applies moves, computes SAN/check/end state, and respects the 10x10 grid boundaries.

nodes.label: RTDB rooms schema
nodes.description: Room records contain metadata, white and black players, boardState, Phase 2-ready cardState, and moveHistory.

nodes.label: Turn-based Firebase Security Rules
nodes.description: Rules require authenticated writers, matching player identity, and a boardState turn transition from white to black or black to white.

nodes.label: useGameSync synchronization hook
nodes.description: Hook subscribes to a room with onValue, reinitializes the engine from FEN, validates local moves, creates atomic RTDB updates, and handles sync errors.

nodes.label: Dark precision UI theme
nodes.description: Dark-mode-first interface uses low-contrast surfaces, high-visibility board and card colors, Inter text, JetBrains Mono data text, and defined board/card color tokens.

nodes.label: 512px PNG piece assets
nodes.description: Piece images are structured by color and type under public/assets/pieces and are intended to support scalable custom pieces and variants.

nodes.label: LoadingAnimation module
nodes.description: Standalone TSX component provides matchmaking, board initialization, and spinner variants with configurable message, size, and styling.

nodes.label: Authentication and game routes
nodes.description: UI routes cover login, lobby, room creation/join/waiting, match, and result screens with access controlled by authentication state.

nodes.label: Pointer and audio feedback
nodes.description: Pointer-field tilt uses animation frames and respects reduced motion/touch; audio provides move, capture, check, castle, and card activation effects.

nodes.label: Phase 1 implementation roadmap
nodes.description: Roadmap covers environment, engine/grid, RTDB synchronization, HUD/audio/UX, and testing/deployment, with listed completion criteria.

nodes.label: Completed architecture decisions
nodes.description: Plan records client-first RTDB rooms/presence, removal of matches and matchmaking queue, client validation plus rules backstop, and empty cardState scaffolding.

nodes.label: Doc-driven development governance
nodes.description: Agent rules require code, data structures, and logic to follow agreed design documents and prohibit unapproved architecture changes.

nodes.label: Stop-on-error protocol
nodes.description: On compile, runtime, or component logic conflicts, work must stop, root cause must be reported, and two or three remedies with trade-offs must be offered.

edges.evidence: README architecture and system document both specify direct Firebase Realtime Database synchronization without a game server.
StandardEngine is explicitly described as the Phase 1 adapter implementing IChessEngine.
The engine produces FEN, turn, check, end-state, and move results represented in room boardState.
The documented hook constructs StandardEngine, initializes it from FEN, and invokes makeMove.
The hook subscribes with onValue and writes atomic updates using Firebase RTDB.
Rules address rooms, players, boardState, moveHistory, cardState, and presence fields defined by the schema.
PLAN states client validation is backed by rules checking player identity and turn changes.
Both specify a centered active 8x8 region inside a 10x10 grid used by the engine.
The documented asset convention names black/bishop.png as a 512x512 piece asset.
The documented asset convention names white/king.png as a 512x512 piece asset.
Piece rendering assets represent the engine positions produced by the standard engine.
Routes describe the browser UI for the client-first application.
index.html links /favicon.svg as the document icon.
The entrypoint loads the React application from /src/main.tsx and the repository includes a React logo asset.
The HTML is a Vite-style module entrypoint and the repository includes vite.svg.
Governance requires implementation to follow agreed architecture documents such as the plan.
Both record Phase 1 completion status and the client-first removal of matchmaking queue/card work to Phase 2.
The license governs the frontend-design skill documentation that specifies the design approach and principles.
